surface: Basic ascent algorithm state and stopping contract
source_issue: The source tests the gradient at an unindexed x, never increments k, uses an invalid do/while rendering, omits the stopping test from the input, does not handle a zero gradient, and outputs x_(k+1) even though the state update is incomplete.
target_action: Rewrote the reader-facing algorithm with x_k throughout, an explicit stopping test, a zero-gradient exit, a strictly improving step, an x_(k+1) assignment, a k increment, and output x_k; distinguished finite termination from convergence.

source_issue: Symmetry and nonsingularity of B_k do not imply that B_k^(-1) grad f is an ascent direction, and the lemma claims a strict inequality even when the gradient is zero.
target_action: Required positive definiteness for the ascent construction, required a nonzero gradient in the lemma, indexed all gradient evaluations by x_k, and separated the local Newton caveat.

source_issue: The source mixes x and x_k, prints a scalar objective as bold f, and discusses a solution without making its assumed existence explicit.
target_action: Used x_k consistently, restored scalar f, stated the existence assumption for delta_k star, and distinguished nondecrease from the strict-increase requirement of the outer algorithm.

source_issue: The bracket definition has the impossible domain b in [0,b], the interpolation statement omits distinct-node and r nonzero conditions, and the Maple listing has unclear or external component rights.
target_action: Required a<b<c and distinct nodes, classified the stationary point by the sign of r, and replaced the excluded Maple listing with independently authored locale-neutral pseudocode; no Maple text or code was copied.

source_issue: The source listing has unclear or external rights, its proposition falsely derives finite bracketing from mere attainment of a maximum, and an unconstrained parabolic proposal need not make quantitative outward progress.
target_action: Supplied independently authored guarded pseudocode with explicit d assignment, d>c, strict-bracket handling, and d-c at least tau(c-b); replaced the theorem by a strict-unimodality and finite-maximizer result whose proof matches the guard and bounded-iteration failure contract.

source_issue: The source identifies x approximately 4.217851814 as a local maximum and omits the second local maximum near 7.131520555.
target_action: Classified approximately 2.900627632 and 7.131520555 as local maxima and approximately 4.217851814 as a local minimum.

surface: Dichotomous search, interval invariant, and example identifier
source_issue: The Maple listing has unclear or external rights, the source proof assumes a half-interval location without establishing the correct comparison invariant or a midpoint error bound consistent with its stopping condition, and the example label occurs after a nested figure caption so it can bind to the figure counter.
target_action: Replaced the listing with independently authored interval pseudocode, treated equality without arbitrary loss of the maximizer, proved that every branch preserves the unique maximizer, paired width at most 2 epsilon with midpoint error at most epsilon, and moved the unchanged example label to the example opening before the nested figure.

source_issue: The source formula can return a negative iteration count when the initial interval already satisfies the tolerance and does not explicitly preserve a maximizer at each contraction.
target_action: Required preservation of at least one maximizer and used max of zero and the logarithmic ceiling for the finite iteration bound.

source_issue: The source delegates the algorithm to an excluded Maple listing and leaves its reuse and stopping behavior implicit.
target_action: Provided independently authored locale-neutral pseudocode with one reused interior evaluation, an explicit width tolerance, a returned best interior point and interval, and hypotheses matching the theorem; no Maple text or code was copied.

source_issue: The source reader depends on five external output fragments generated by legacy implementations, while the Indonesian fragment must remain closed without importing excluded program code.
target_action: Integrated the relevant numerical values directly as clearly identified source-output witnesses, removed all translated-target input dependencies, and retained no legacy code or unsupported claim that the revised bridges reproduce an identical trace.

source_issue: The source delegates the executable surface to an excluded Maple listing and conflates derivative-residual and positional stopping criteria.
target_action: Replaced it with independently authored pseudocode that maintains derivative-sign endpoints, separates derivative and interval tolerances, returns explicit evidence, and reports iteration-limit failure rather than claiming convergence.

source_issue: The source theorem merely states that some unspecified delta exists for every input epsilon, and its proof does not establish a quantitative derivative-to-distance implication under ordinary concavity.
target_action: Proved the maximizer-set interval invariant and geometric width bound for concave C1 functions, separated exact-root, positional, and derivative-residual exits, and made the quantitative distance conclusion conditional on strong concavity.

source_issue: The source exercise assumes strict concavity but divides by the unknown absolute Hessian at an intermediate point; strict concavity alone supplies no uniform positive curvature modulus.
target_action: Required m-strong concavity, equivalently phi double-prime at most -m, and derived the valid bound |u-x star| less than epsilon_g over m; retained the bilipschitz alternative as a separate exercise.

surface: One-dimensional Newton step and executable bridge
source_issue: The Taylor expansion evaluates its derivatives at x_0 while claiming to expand about x_k, and the source delegates execution to an excluded Maple listing without explicit denominator or convergence-failure handling.
target_action: Evaluated both derivatives at x_k, retained the correct Newton update, and supplied independently authored pseudocode with derivative and step tolerances, a zero-Hessian failure, a curvature classification, and no global-convergence overclaim.

source_issue: The source selects a maximal derivative magnitude without explicitly using continuity and compactness to prove that the maximum exists and is strictly below one.
target_action: Used continuity of f prime on compact S to define q as the attained maximum and invoked the pointwise strict bound to obtain q less than one before applying the mean-value theorem.

source_issue: The source proof stops after calling rho a contraction and never invokes the contraction conclusion or proves that its fixed point solves h=0; it also changes a non-strict derivative lower bound into a strict one.
target_action: Kept zero at most rho prime at most q, proved rho maps S into itself, invoked the contraction lemma for unique convergence, and used gamma positive to make the fixed-point identity equivalent to h(x star)=0.

surface: Maximization specialization of the generic theorem
source_issue: The source sets h=phi prime and gamma=1 over phi double-prime, which makes both h prime and gamma negative for a strictly concave maximization problem and therefore contradicts the theorem hypotheses.
target_action: Set h=-phi prime and gamma=-1 over phi double-prime, preserving the Newton map x-phi prime over phi double-prime while satisfying positivity under phi double-prime less than zero.

source_issue: The source contains an undefined mathbb{x} symbol, allows unrestricted real p and nonzero real alpha, and does not impose the standard alpha less than one condition for linear convergence.
target_action: Used the vector limit x star, required p at least one and positive finite alpha, added alpha less than one when p equals one, and retained the linear, superlinear, and quadratic classifications.

source_issue: The source writes phi(x star)=x star instead of f(x star)=x star, claims bounded f prime alone controls a ratio containing h prime in the denominator, concludes exact order two from only an upper quadratic estimate, and ties the rate claim to global contraction hypotheses whose Newton specialization forces h double-prime at the root to vanish.
target_action: Separated the standard local Newton-rate theorem from the stronger global contraction theorem, assumed h is C2 near a simple root and that the Newton iterates converge, used the exact Taylor remainder to prove a finite Q-quadratic constant, and distinguished exact order two when h double-prime at the root is nonzero from a zero quadratic ratio otherwise.

source_issue: Several labels appear after an inner numbered equation or nested figure caption, so references named as a corollary, example, definition, or theorem can inherit the wrong counter.
target_action: Kept every identifier unchanged but placed cor:QuadFitTurn, ex:DichotSearchExample, def:Contraction, and thm:NMPreReq immediately after their owning environment opens, before any nested counter-changing surface.

surface: Golden-section failure example and figure caption
source_issue: The source and first target draft describe the piecewise function as non-unimodal, but it is weakly unimodal: it rises to the unique global maximum, falls, has a long lower plateau, and then falls again. The actual failure mechanism is the one-sided equality branch when both probes land on that plateau.
target_action: Characterized the function as weakly but not strictly unimodal, identified the plateau equality tie as the branch that can discard the global maximizer, and corrected the figure caption without changing the source numerical witness.
